componentAcceptance: All T27 criteria are covered. Existing refs/open/snapshot/Unicode fill/click and stale-target denial remain. browser_script evaluates bounded script only inside the authorized page with bounded JSON results. browser_upload supplies at most 1 MiB of in-memory bytes to a DOM input and never opens a disk path. Internal navigation/fetch remains under the origin allowlist and route interception. The product remote_computer_browser tool exposes open/snapshot/click/type/script/upload/download/close with Bot/machine/root grants and stable task/attempt plus per-action operation IDs.
productAcceptance: T27 passes at integration level. Local and remote browser navigation, DOM refs, script and controlled uploads work through the real AgentLoop; downloads and internal-address policy remain enforced. Formal scores are 0/20 work packages, 29/63 scenarios and M0 11/12.
implementation: Added browser_script with input/result bounds and browser_upload with strict base64, filename, MIME and 1 MiB validation.
Registered the new Agent protocol tools in the Host machine ceiling and product grant composition.
Added remote_computer_browser with stable task/attempt identity, unique operation IDs and execution-time machine authorization; visibility alone never grants execution.
testRuns: npm run integration:probe-remote-agent-browser: all 11 checks pass, including script, in-memory upload, 1 MiB+1 refusal and internal fetch denial.
npm run integration:probe-product-default: all 45 checks pass. The real AgentLoop opens, scripts and closes the remote browser with the same task/attempt and three succeeded operations.
Final npm test: phase one 1593/1589/0/4 and phase two 387/303/0/84; total 1980 tests, 1892 pass, 0 fail, 88 skipped. npm run check:client: OK.
preservedFailures: The generic product tool was initially hidden by the legacy remote_computer visibility filter. It is now discoverable while machines.call still enforces execution grants.
The final machine.bind initially omitted browser tools; the fixture now uses the same complete approved tool ceiling. A separate missing operationId was fixed in the product adapter.

The offline fixture initially read nested browserSessionId/result fields incorrectly and used a non-executed async function shape. These test assertions were corrected after inspecting actual receipts; browser operations themselves were not weakened.
limitations: Scripts are powerful page-context code and therefore remain behind the explicit browser grant; no arbitrary Node.js or filesystem execution is provided.
The local browser build may differ from a distribution-pinned build. OS browser dependencies and protected cross-machine deployment remain separate gates.
No production browser profile, real model inference, push or release was used.
